subject: Re: MAP alignment — acceptance conditions, exit gates & canary sprint

Subject: MAP alignment — acceptance conditions, exit gates & canary sprint

Hi Natalie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together a concise mutual action plan (attached) with the evaluation acceptance conditions we typically use for MAP-driven pilots. Key asks:

- Confirm the acceptance test owners on your side and the initial validation window (we suggested 2 weeks).
- Confirm whether SOC2 evidence is sufficient (we attached the snapshot) or if you need any additional artifacts for procurement.
- Agree on a short canary sprint (3 business days) to validate latency/p99 and basic failover before we scale the Dedicated pool.

High-level acceptance criteria in the draft:
- Functional: 95% of prompts return context-aware responses matching your evaluation prompt set (tracked via test harness).
- Performance: p95 latency < 400ms for 1–2k token generation, sustained throughput >= 50 requests/sec per model variant.
- Quality: no more than 3% hallucination rate on the accuracy test slice tied to your clinical prompts.
- Security/ops: KV retention TTL confirmed; audit log delivery to your S3 bucket for the validation window.

I attached the MAP (rdw-map-v1.pdf) and the proposed test plan grid (clearpath-eval-test-plan.xlsx). Can you review and indicate any non-starters by EOD Wednesday so we can lock the canary dates?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Accounts — Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Kimberly —

Appreciate the crisp MAP. A few notes from procurement and security:

1) Procurement would like the SOC2 snapshot but will still need a signed MSA or a vendor questionnaire completed. I attached the questionnaire outline we usually use (see procurement@clearpathhealth.com).
2) For acceptance tests, the quality threshold (3% hallucination) looks reasonable but can we add an upper bound for response variance on the clinical normalization test? Our clinical safety team expects reproducible normalizations within a defined token edit distance.
3) Can the audit logs be exported to our secure bucket within 24 hours of each test run?

We are generally aligned with the canary idea. If you can provide test accounts + the harness instructions, we can schedule the validation window the week of Sep 13.

—Natalie

Subject: Re: MAP alignment — acceptance conditions, exit gates & canary sprint

Hi all —

Thanks for the fast feedback, Natalie. I've updated the MAP grid in the attached workbook to incorporate:
- A reproducibility metric for the clinical normalization test (median token edit distance <= 4 across 50 canonical prompts).
- An explicit audit log SLA: logs delivered to ClearPath S3 within 24 hours of each test, retained for 90 days (we can extend on request).
- Canary run plan: 3 business days with the following gating checks each night: performance stability (p95 variance < 15%), error rate < 0.5%, and no regression on the safety-labeled prompts.

Exit gates (go/no-go):
1) Functional sign-off: Engineering PM (ClearPath) confirms >= 95% pass on critical prompt slice.
2) Performance sign-off: p95 < 400ms and sustained throughput >= 50rps for 3 consecutive 1-hour windows during canary.
3) Security sign-off: SOC2 snapshot reviewed + audit log delivery verified.
4) Commercial: PO or committed contract in place for initial Dedicated capacity (minimum 3-month commit).

If any gate fails, the rollback plan is: pause Dedicated provisioning, switch traffic to hosted API with throttles, and run a 48-hour remediation sprint. We captured owners in the sheet (column: "owner").

Next actions I can take this week: create the test accounts, share the harness runbook, and seed the DocuSign envelope for the MAP so procurement can review. Kimberly — confirm if we should include a 10% initial discount for the Dedicated commit or leave pricing to the AE.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
